title: SubjectAssertionClaims
description: Claims of a short-lived ES256 assertion signed by OpenVibe.Network that says a person allowed one service to act for them on another service (ADR-003, amendment 2026-11-06; plan H1). Minted only from the person's own Network access token (POST /internal/subject-assertions): without that token nothing is signed. Carried on a money call in X-OV-Subject-Assertion. The signature key is published in Network's JWKS (kid ov-network-assertion-1, kty EC, alg ES256) beside the RS256 session key, so a receiver verifies it offline.

iss.description: Issuer; https://openvibe.network in production. The receiver checks it against the issuer it expects.

sub.description: The person the assertion is about: their canonical subject. The receiver refuses an assertion that does not name the person the route acts for.

aud.description: The service(s) the assertion is for. A receiver accepts it only when its own audience is in the list. A list is used when the assertion travels a chain (a tip goes from the site to Tips and on to Billing).

act.description: The service the assertion was minted for (the one that held the person's token). It is the only service that may present it, unless `for` names others.

for.description: The services that may carry the assertion (the minting service is always in it). A receiver presented by a service that is not in this list refuses the assertion (403 assertion.actor_mismatch).

jti.description: Unique per assertion. A receiver remembers the jtis it has seen for the replay window and refuses a second use (403 assertion.replayed).

exp.description: Expires at (seconds since the epoch). The assertion lives 60 seconds.

nbf.description: Not before (seconds since the epoch). Optional; a receiver forgives a small clock difference.
